rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so this candidate keeps all seven passes but shifts weights toward aggressiveness on security and diversity while holding cost tolerances below the levels that would risk blowup on a 190-byte, 4-function binary. SUB and SPLIT get high weights on every dimension because they are cheap, low-risk, and SPLIT creates additional basic blocks that increase the attack surface available to FLA, BCF, and IBR on this program's few small functions. FLA and BCF keep high SecurityGain (0.8) to maximize control-flow confusion in the 109-byte main, but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost tolerances stay moderate (0.35-0.45) so the selector still prefers them only where features justify the blowup rather than forcing them into the tiny 21-22 byte helper methods where flattening overhead dominates. IBR and ICALL sit in the middle: indirect branches and calls add meaningful disassembly/resistance diversity for modest cost, and the virtual-style True/False member functions give ICALL something to work with. IGV stays lowest since this program has minimal global state, so its expected diversity payoff is small; keeping it enabled at modest weight lets it apply only where features favor it. CorrectnessRisk weights remain at or above 0.5 across the board since round 0 showed no ICE or miscompile, leaving headroom to escalate further in later rounds if measurements stay clean.
